findings.title: [P2] Inconclusive persisted-number verification loses its public catalog error
findings.rationale:
Source-confirmed counterexample, not a request executed by this reviewer: take an authorized official channel with its exact current owner/credential and a persisted phone not present on the first two current WABA pages, where page two still returns a valid next cursor. The new method deliberately stops after one debug request plus two phone pages and throws MetaIndisponivelError at meta.client.ts:153. Malformed/oversized/cyclic cursor paths throw the same type at lines 121-122,150-157. This is the expected safe inconclusive branch of the new bounded contract, rather than resource-not-found or successful convergence.

That class extends plain Error and adds only code/detalhe (meta.client.ts:33-35); it is neither a Nest HttpException nor an HTTP error with statusCode. ChannelsService.verificar awaits it at channels.service.ts:287 and has only a finally lease release at 344-345, with no translation. ChannelsController.verificar simply returns that promise at channels.controller.ts:86-91. AppModule registers only the Prisma-specific BancoAtrasadoFilter (app.module.ts:39; banco-atrasado.filter.ts:19). The installed public Nest BaseExceptionFilter source, read only at node_modules/@nestjs/core/exceptions/base-exception-filter.js:16-17,34-46,62-64, sends this unknown Error as generic HTTP 500 with an Internal server error message and no code field. Therefore the class's internal META_INDISPONIVEL property never reaches the BFF caller.

Why now: cp36c newly establishes budget/cursor exhaustion as a normal deliberate verification outcome and explicitly promises a safe catalogued inconclusive error. The channel module's verify contract requires provider failures to map to application catalog codes (integrations-and-channels.md:28), under D-05/D-07's explicit recoverable failures and separate observations. The older generic Meta error plumbing predates this patch; this finding concerns the newly material bounded outcome at the changed verify locus, not a broad reopening of historically accepted integration architecture. Adapter unit tests at meta.client.spec.ts:173-193 assert only toBeInstanceOf(MetaIndisponivelError), and the green PG lifecycle covers a successful second page, so neither tests the actual failure envelope. No credential leakage, tenant bypass or persisted status mutation is demonstrated; the response is safe but fails its approved public error contract and hides a legitimate inconclusive result as an internal server failure.
findings.suggested_action:
Recommend A: translate only the recognized MetaIndisponivelError at the existing verify application/transport boundary into HTTP 503 with the fixed safe catalog code META_INDISPONIVEL and a constant inconclusive/unavailable message. Keep the outgoing adapter/domain error separate from HTTP policy where practical. Preserve existing HttpException/auth/CAS exceptions, exact owner/currentAttempt/generation/epoch/receipt predicates, no network under transactions and the finally lease release. Add real BFF/Nest/PostgreSQL negative coverage that asserts status plus catalog code and proves unchanged credential/attempt version/identity/receipt/channel observations and released lease; retain the real adapter's exact request-budget and cursor tests. Effort small; risk low with a type-specific mapping; blast radius the verify caller and scoped test; maintenance low; no new query/network cost; elegance and structural soundness improve by completing the already owned boundary.

B: add a broad/global typed provider-error filter for every Meta consumer. It could be coherent under a separately admitted scope, but has larger blast radius and retest/maintenance burden and offers no performance advantage for this narrow correction; it is unnecessary here. C: leave generic HTTP 500. Zero implementation effort and no performance cost, but the new deliberate inconclusive outcome remains indistinguishable from a programming failure and violates the existing catalog contract; not recommended. Neither a blanket catch-all, a 200/null fallback, relaxed provider proof nor declaring the adapter unit green is a valid substitute. Root owns admission, classification, implementation and final disposition.
